overview.description: Competitive patience in which two or more players each play the same solitaire layout (typically Klondike) at the same time; the first to complete their layout wins.

history.origins: Competitive patiences date to the late 19th century; any single-player patience can be played by two or more players in competition, each with their own layout.
timeline: Late 19th century: competitive patiences documented; any single-player patience played in competition by two or more players.
history.evolution: Played informally as a race; no formal tournament history.
history.cultural: Popular as a parlor race in Europe and North America; often played with Klondike.

setup.players: Two or more players; each needs their own deck and table space.
setup.dealing: Each player deals their own deck into the chosen layout (e.g. Klondike: seven tableau columns with one to seven cards, first card face-up; remainder as stock).

rules.objective: Be the first player to complete your solitaire layout by moving all cards to the foundations (or otherwise satisfying the chosen layout's win condition).
rules.gameplay: All players start at the same time and play the same patience game (e.g. Klondike) on their own layout. There are no turns; everyone plays simultaneously. Legal moves are those of the underlying patience (e.g. build down in alternating color on the tableau, build up in suit on foundations, turn stock as allowed). The first to finish wins.
keyRules: Each player has an identical layout and deck.
All players play at once; no turn order.
Legal moves follow the underlying patience rules (e.g. Klondike).
First player to complete their layout wins.

strategy.basic: Play the same layout as your opponents; speed matters. Clear aces and deuces to foundations early.
strategy.intermediate: Balance building on tableau with filling foundations; avoid blocking key cards.
strategy.advanced: Memorize common Klondike dead-ends; prioritize moves that free the most cards.
tips: Agree on the layout (e.g. Klondike) and stock-turn rule (one or three cards) before starting.

list.name: Klondike
list.description: Use standard Klondike layout: seven tableau columns, four foundations, build down alternating color on tableau, up in suit on foundations; turn stock one or three at a time.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses default engine; no overrides needed for Klondike layout.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
